chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:
I asked al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام about the ghusl of the deceased: is there in it the wudu (ablution) of salat (prayer), or not?

He said: “The ghusl of the deceased is begun with his joints, so he is washed with al-ḥuruḍ, then his face and head are washed with sidr, then water is poured over him three times. He must not be washed except in a shirt; a man puts his hand inside it and pours over him from above it. And he places in the water some sidr and some camphor. He must not press his abdomen unless he fears something nearby, in which case he wipes with a gentle wiping without pressing. Then the one who washed him washes his hand up to the shoulders three times before shrouding him, then when he has shrouded him, he performs ghusl.”

key_terms.بِالسِّدْرِ: with sidr, used in washing the deceased
key_terms.غُسْلُ اَلْمَيِّتِ: the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.كَافُورٍ: camphor added to the washing water

ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for ghusl of the deceased in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal instructions for the ghusl of the deceased, describing the order of washing, the substances used, and the manner of handling the body. It also mentions the washing and ghusl required of the person who performs the washing, making it an important text in funerary fiqh.
